items.title: David Murray interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 18, 2003
items.q: I was getting into John Coltrane and Sonny Rollins and all these people, and I was putting that into the church.

ctx.x: But the idea that you’re playing improvised music but you can’t play jazz. Your mother didn’t like that. What was the distinction?

Well as long as I was playing the church music and improvising it wasn’t considered jazz. Like I mean I was getting into John Coltrane and Sonny Rollins and all these people, and I was putting that into the church. They didn’t know I was really getting into that. All they knew was that as long as I could play the church melodies fine, whatever else I played, they didn’t care. They didn’t even know if it was jazz or not. They didn’t care. But they knew that it was good. But they knew that when it came to playing…
Did you retain the faith part of the church?
